newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor probed for misuse of public funds.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor probed for misuse of public funds.

text.p: Paris's Gaullist mayor Jean Tiberi vowed on Thursday to stay in his job despite being investigated, together with his wife, on suspicion of misusing public funds.

Tiberi, who succeeded Jacques Chirac as mayor of the French capital when his mentor was elected president in 1995, said he was being formally probed over a payment made to his wife out of public funds and paid into the couple's joint bank account.
"It is being wrongly alleged that I intervened to have my wife hired by the Essone (an area near Paris) General Council," Tiberi said in a statement.
He said neither he nor his wife had anything to reproach themselves with, and "I will carry on with my mission".
The case came as a fresh blow for Tiberi, who has come under fire in a housing scandal and a probe into suspected illicit funding of his Gaullist RPR party by Paris' housing authority.

The Paris city hall said Tiberi was being investigated on suspicion of being an accomplice to misuse of public funds. His wife Xaviere was formally placed under investigation last December on suspicion of misusing public funds.
Investigators say they suspect she received 200,000 francs ($40,000) from the Essone elected council for a 36-page report largely copied out of a book.

Xavier Dugoin, Gaullist president of the council, is also being investigated for allegedly paying the sum to Mrs Tiberi. He was reported to have told investigators that Tiberi himself decided the amount to be paid to his wife.

The case led to a much-publicised episode in which Gaullist Justice Minister Jacques Toubon ordered a helicopter to be chartered to track down a magistrate holidaying in Nepal, in an effort to head off the probe of Mrs Tiberi which was being pursued in the magistrate's absence by an independent-minded deputy.
Tiberi said he has been harassed by magistrates, media and political opponents since he took over from Chirac.

"Over the past six months, this campaign has become a real manhunt: my private life and that of my family have been searched, my bank accounts have been scrutinised...my name has been besmirched, my wife lowly insulted," he said.

Investigating magistrate Eric Halphen searched Tiberi's home last year in a probe into illicit RPR financing through a false invoicing system and alleged rigged public works tenders in the Paris region.
More than a dozen businessmen and former housing officials were formally placed under investigation in the case.

The probe also led to a scandal after criminal police chief Olivier Foll ordered his officers to refuse to assist in the search of Tiberi's home. A court later deprived Foll of his investigative capacity.
Tiberi has also come under attack in a housing scandal after his son Dominique was found to rent a flat, lavishly renovated at public expense, from the city hall while letting out his own home.
Tiberi has insisted the decision to grant his son the flat was a coincidence and he played no part in it. He has filed a suit against persons unknown for violating judicial secrecy.
The Paris prosecutor decided against prosecuting Tiberi over his son's apartment, triggering charges from the Socialist opposition that the government was using procedural tricks to shield him.
